criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Four frames hold up. Slide 1 has a lit 6061 part with two shadowed pockets in the vise and the end mill held clear. Slide 4 has a pool of light in the aisle with a full-length machinist for scale. Slide 6 puts 24 cyan taped bays beside the 100 at one pitch. Slide 9 shows empty bays at standing eye, with a worker and four Lockheed enclosures behind. The other five frames each lean on a primitive or a diagram, and the 7 descriptor allows one. Slide 3 is 13 rows of 24 tiny parts (312, which matches parts_per_employee). At 432 px it reads as a spreadsheet texture with no single subject, and the second tray fades into grey. Slide 5 shows 100 roofs at a sheared oblique that reads as dominoes or a checkerboard, and the right half of the frame is dead black. Slide 8's pendant is a rounded box with a calculator keypad in front of a flat navy wall. Slide 2 is a mid-grey slab grid and a flat grey pour square, the grey-middle diagram look. Slide 7 is a flat cyanotype sheet with a flat grey part plate, and machine_qa warns its lower zone is weak. The measured scale is honest: on slide 2 the square sides measure 0.369 and 0.340 of the slab against sqrt(100k/735k) and sqrt(85k/735k). No frame passes the showstopper test.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: This is clearly one deck: one dark machine-shop world in graphite and 6061. The part motif changes state across the deck: finished in the vise on 1, multiplied on 3, standing on its drawing on 7, absent from the bays on 9. The cyan accent marks only Hadrian's cell, on 6, 7 and 9. Slide 6 is slide 5's bench plus one block, so that cut is the declared turn. The value track stays dark throughout. What sits outside: slide 8's flat navy backdrop and slide 7's blue sheet bring a cool blue the rest of the deck doesn't carry. Slide 4's overhead pool contradicts the declared low west key.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. 300, 735,000, 100,000, 85,000, 24, 2027, 30, 100, 800, 250,000 and 2,000 are all in figures.json. 2026 and October 14th trace to the quotes in c11 and c6. The sources are primary: the Lockheed release, hadrian.co and TDLR for Dallas County. Several phrasings are looser than their sources, and the worst sits on the turn frame. (1) Slide 8 paraphrases c16 as 'brings its automation, software and training inside Lockheed'. It drops 'from our own factories', the one link the record makes between Hadrian's software and Lockheed, while slide 7 attributes Opus, which Hadrian calls AI powered (c21), to the software in its own factories. Read together, the sources say more than the deck admits. (2) Slide 7's attribution 'Hadrian, on its own factories' is narrower than the run's own rejected entry, and the deck leaves out c22: Hadrian deploys manufacturing cells in either Hadrian facilities or customer sites. (3) Slide 3 divides 2025's 250,000 parts by the currently employed nearly 800 and draws it as one employee's share, mixing two time bases during an expansion. (4) Slide 1's headline 'due in 2027' is harder than 'expected to be operational in early 2027'. (5) The caption's 'Hadrian calls its own factories AI powered' rests on c24, which first_comment.txt doesn't list. None of this is fabrication, but (1) changes what a reader believes.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened: Lockheed's October 14th release, a $300M Grand Prairie expansion and Hadrian's 24-machine cell, who runs it (Lockheed's own workforce), where (Grand Prairie, Dallas County via c34) and when (early 2027). There is no decision by any public body, and nothing a reader can do next. The AI stake is stated only as an absence. The 2,000 jobs are handled honestly as a statewide company figure, but they give the reader nothing concrete.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover names the news. The 5 to 6 pair is the best move in the deck: the same bench, plus the 24 as empty bays. 7 and 8 turn the deck toward the AI question, and 9 closes on who runs the cell and when. Slide 3 is cuttable without loss, and slide 2 is setup that delays the cell. The close lands on a fact and leaves the question to the caption, so the turn on 8 never returns on 9.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: 'The release gives AI no job description.' is a strong, specific opener. The fragments 'Announced.' and 'Already done, by Lockheed's count.' give the caption a clear ledger structure. 'The deck runs from a finished part to 24 empty bays.' is meta. 'Drawn to illustrate.' repeats on the deks. There is little regional texture beyond Grand Prairie and Dallas County. No house-rule breaks.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The world is new: a machine shop in graphite and 6061 with a cold cyan accent, against no. 55's floodlit OR, no. 54's brush country and no. 53's tissue reliefs. The counting moves repeat the last two decks: no. 55 shipped 25 lids in 41 taped bays and a 339-unit isotype wall, and this deck ships 24 empty taped bays and a 312-unit isotype tray. No. 54 shipped a block beside the projected plant's slots at the same pitch, and slide 6 is the same block-beside-block at one pitch. The cover opens on a hero object close-up, like no. 55's wall camera. No topic repeat in the 30-day window.

one_sentence_fix: On slide 8, quote Hadrian's chief in full, the automation, software and workforce training from our own factories directly inside Lockheed Martin, and set it beside Hadrian's own offer to deploy cells at customer sites (c22), so the deck asks its open question against the strongest link the record makes.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Seen straight down, 312 parts in 13 rows of 24 read as a grey spreadsheet texture at 432 px. There is no single subject, the lifted part is a speck at top right, and the second tray fades into the mid tones.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Put the lifted part on the bench lit by the west key as the one subject, let the tray fall off away from it, and drop the second tray.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The pendant is a primitive rounded box with a calculator keypad, hung in front of a flat navy wall that belongs to no other frame. The huge black screen is a dead zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model a real CNC pendant with override knobs and a handwheel, replace the navy wall with the machine's graphite enclosure, and rake the warm low key across the key edges from the left.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The 100 roofs sit at a sheared oblique that reads as dominoes or a checkerboard rather than machines. The right half of the frame is empty black.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Give each roof a stack light and a pendant arm with long casts running right down the aisles, and fill the empty half.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A mid-grey slab grid with a flat grey pour square reads as graph paper sitting in the grey middle. The rolled carpet corner is the only relief.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Darken the slab to near-black sealed concrete with saw-cut joints caught only on their edges, and let the pour's timber form boards and the rolled carpet throw long casts so the pour is the one bright plane.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The cyanotype sheet and the part are both flat plates seen from above, and machine_qa flags a weak lower zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Let the part stand with visible height on its own plan view and cast across the views, and run the sheet off the bottom and side edges.
